text:
devon: FYI seeing a weird IOPS "ping-pong" in us-west3 causing GPU attach latency spikes. noticed after last overlayfs rollout.
aj: reproduction? a job id or node id?
maria: +1 node id and timeline please.
devon: node gnode-uw3-238, started ~14:02 UTC. attaching logs: dmesg shows intermittent blk_update_request: I/O error, then normal, then error again every ~9s. GPU attach requests backlogged.
ops-bot: ALERT: nvme_iops_spike detected on gnode-uw3-238 (metric spike 4.5x baseline) — runbook: /runbooks/nvme-iops-flicker
aj: can you paste the exact dmesg snippet?
devon: here —
```
[14:02:18] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 1234567
[14:02:27] nvme: I/O 0x1234 timeout
[14:02:27] blk_update_request: read error, dev nvme0n1
[14:02:36] I/O completed ok
[14:02:45] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 1234999
```
liam: that periodicity ~9s matches the cleaner/trim cron we rolled out in ap-sched last week. maybe cleaner is colliding with heavy small-R/W workloads.
sofia: we did change overlayfs mount flags in the rollout — could be causing more write-amplification with small files.
maria: can we temporarily mute the cleaner on this host? devon — can you put a temp tag to skip janitor?
devon: requested a skip tag: `janitor:skip=1` on gnode-uw3-238. will monitor.
ben: is this hitting only ephemeral? any SMART wear counters changing?
devon: SMART shows rising media_errors and an increasing bad block count on nvme0, but not full failure. serial: NVME-ABC-238. wear_level 71% -> 72% over last 12h.
aj: if wear + write amplification -> we should avoid scrub/warmup on that host and move GPUs off.
liam: propose two-step mitigation: 1) skip janitor on affected nodes, 2) drain high-churn batch jobs from gnode-uw3-238 to spare pool (takes ~3min), 3) throttle small-IO jobs via ioprio or cgroup.
devon: started drain; migrating 4 pending gpu jobs -> spare-pool-us-west3.
sofia: rolling back overlayfs flag would be higher risk right now (global). prefer local mitigations first.
maria: tagging oncall — @liam are you able to take lead for the next hour?
liam: taking it. will watch metrics and coordinate with storage team.
ops-bot: NOTE: auto-migration triggered for 4 jobs (job-9823..job-9826) -> spare-pool-us-west3
ben: if this repeats, we should consider preemptive replacement for the nvme (warranty?) and add the node to a watchlist.
devon: agree. filed infra ticket INFRA-4521 with SMART dump and timeline.
aj: thanks — after drain, can you run `fio` microbench (4k randrw) with low runtime to validate? post results here.
devon: running fio now, will paste output in 2m.
liam: rough cost note — migrating jobs and extra scheduling will bump GPU reservation churn, but better than attach failures. be conservative with migrations.
devon: fio result: 4k randrw 70% r/30% w, iops ~12k stable when janitor skipped, drops to ~1.8k when janitor runs. attaching snippet.
```
fio --name=randrw --rw=randrw --bs=4k --size=1G --runtime=30
IOPS: 12000   lat p95 12ms
# after janitor run
IOPS: 1800    lat p95 120ms
```
sofia: confirmed correlation. liam please coordinate with storage to adjust cleaner cadence and add jitter to avoid synchronized bursts.
liam: will open STOR-364 to add jitter + backoff and recommend changing overlayfs flags in a staged canary.
maria: thanks everyone. update if anything changes. :thumbsup:"
